s1.expectation: I am inside the channel called general, in a server called Accessibility Testin's server, with nothing written in it yet.
s1.cue: The top line says '# general' next to a back arrow, the big bold welcome names 'Accessibility Testin's server', and the box at the bottom says 'Message #general'.

first_pass.why: The channel name sits at the top where I look first, and the same name is repeated in the message box, so I can check myself twice without doubt. The page is mostly white space, which helps me.

s2.expectation: I am in the general channel of Accessibility Testin's server. It looks exactly like an empty channel.
s2.cue: '# general' at the top, 'Welcome to Accessibility Testin's server' in large type, and 'Message #general' in the typing box.

first_pass.why: The name of the place is at the top and repeated at the bottom. Nothing competes with it.

s3.where: Channel list of Accessibility Testin's server
s3.expectation: I am looking at the list of channels inside Accessibility Testin's server, and 'general' is the one currently chosen.
s3.cue: The heading 'Accessibility Testin's server', the grey highlight behind '# general', and the blue tile in the left column.

first_pass.why: The heading tells me the server, but the left column has three tiles that all say exactly 'ATs'. Only one is blue. If I had three servers with the same letters I could not tell by looking which one I am in; I would have to trust the heading and keep checking it. The column of rounded squares with no words is hard for me to remember.
first_pass.solution: Put the full server name under or beside each tile in the left column, or at least make the tiles look different from one another, so the selected one is named and not only coloured.

test_cases.action: On the page with the column of 'ATs' squares down the left, tap each 'ATs' square in turn (not the + at the bottom). After each tap, say which server you are in, using only what the screen shows.
test_cases.real_if: nothing on the screen lets you tell the squares apart or say which one you are in
test_cases.not_real_if: something on the screen tells them apart and says which one you are in
test_cases.observed_result: I tapped each of the four 'ATs' squares in turn. Each tap turned that square blue and moved the small dark bar beside it, and that was the only change. All four times the heading said exactly 'Accessibility Testin's server', with the same '# general' and 'General' underneath. Nothing on the screen told the four apart. If I had to say which server I was in, I could only say 'the third one from the top', and I could not have said what makes it different from the second.

s3.closing_comment: On the phone all four squares say 'ATs' and every one of them opens a page headed 'Accessibility Testin's server' with the same channels. It is not just hard to tell which square I am on; there is literally nothing on screen that distinguishes them.

s4.expectation: I am in the Messages area, where my private conversations with people would be. I have none yet.
s4.cue: The large heading 'Messages' at the top, and the speech bubble tile at the top left is the blue, selected one.

first_pass.why: The heading is one plain word that says exactly what the page is. The illustration is large but it is below the heading and does not stop me.

first_pass.solution: Label each server tile with its full name, or give each a distinct picture, so the one I am in is named and not only coloured blue.

s6.where: Create Your Server - choose how to start
s6.expectation: I am at the beginning of making a new server, choosing whether to make my own or start from a template.
s6.cue: The large heading 'Create Your Server' and the sentence under it, plus 'Start from a template'.

first_pass.why: The heading says exactly what I am doing. The choices are in a simple list with words next to each picture. I do not know how many steps follow, but I know where I am right now.

s7.where: Tell Us More About Your Server
s7.expectation: I am part-way through making a new server, and it is asking whether the server is for friends or for a club.
s7.cue: The heading 'Tell Us More About Your Server' and the words 'your new server' in the line under it.

first_pass.why: The heading names the question, not the task. It does not say 'Create Your Server' any more, and there is no step count, so I have to work out from 'your new server' that I am still in the same process. I do not know if this is step two of three or two of ten.
first_pass.solution: Keep 'Create Your Server' visible as the task name and add a step indicator such as 'Step 2 of 3', so I know which process this belongs to and how far along I am.

test_cases.action: Tap the + at the bottom of the left column of squares. Tap 'Create My Own', then 'For me and my friends'. On each page, say which task you are doing and which step of it you are on. Do not press 'Create Server'. Leave with the back arrow or X until you are back where you started.
test_cases.real_if: on a page you cannot tell which task or which step you are on
test_cases.not_real_if: every page tells you the task and the step
test_cases.observed_result: I tapped the + at the bottom of the squares. Page 1 was titled 'Create Your Server', so the task is creating a server, but there is no step number. I tapped 'Create My Own'. Page 2 was titled 'Tell Us More About Your Server' and mentioned 'your new server'. I can infer it is still the same task, but there is no step number and the task name has gone. I tapped 'For me and my friends'. Page 3 was titled 'Create Your Server' again, word for word the same as page 1, with 'Server Name' already filled in with 'Accessibility Testin's server' and the 'Create Server' button, which I did not press. No page told me which step I was on or how many there were. And because pages 1 and 3 share a title, the title alone cannot tell me whether I went forward or back. The back arrows took me back one page at a time, then the X returned me to the server page.

s7.closing_comment: Confirmed on the device: no step indicator on any of the three pages, the middle page drops the task name, and the first and last pages share the identical title 'Create Your Server'.

test_cases.action: Open the 'general' room (tap an 'ATs' square, then '# general'). Tap the magnifying glass at the top-right. Type the word hello and nothing else. Look away for a few seconds, look back, and say where you are. Leave with the back arrow.
test_cases.real_if: nothing on the screen tells you that you are searching, and in which room
test_cases.not_real_if: you can say from the screen that you are searching, and where
test_cases.observed_result: I opened '# general' and tapped the magnifying glass. The box at the top showed a grey chip 'in: general' before my cursor, with tabs such as Members, Media and Pins under it. I typed hello. The chip 'in: general' stayed in the box beside my word, and the page said 'We searched far and wide. Unfortunately, no results were found.' When I looked back after a pause, I could say that I was searching, and that it was in general, from the chip plus that sentence. The back arrow returned me to '# general'.

s32.closing_comment: The 'in: general' chip stays in the box after typing, and the 'We searched far and wide' line confirms I am searching. It is still shorthand I have to decode, but it does tell me the task and the room.

s33.where: Finish setting up your server panel, over the general channel
s33.expectation: A panel has slid up over the general channel listing the four steps to finish setting up my server; I have done none.
s33.cue: The heading 'Finish setting up your server!' and 'You have completed 0 of 4 steps.', with '# general' dimmed behind.

first_pass.why: It names the task, tells me how many steps there are and how many I have done. This is exactly the kind of progress statement I rely on.

s35.expectation: I am making a new thread inside the general channel.

first_pass.why: The heading says what I am doing and the line under it says where. That pair is exactly what I need.

s36.expectation: I am on a page for buying Nitro as a gift for someone.

s43.expectation: I think I am looking at trending GIFs to send in the general channel.
s43.cue: The small word 'Trending' with a back arrow, 'GIFs' shaded above it, and '# general' dimmed at the very top.

first_pass.why: Almost the whole screen is a wall of pictures of faces and animals and big decorative words, all shouting at once. I cannot recognise faces, and this many images shuts me down before I find the small word 'Trending'. I would stop here.
first_pass.solution: Make the heading much larger, for example 'Trending GIFs for #general', and show fewer, smaller previews with plenty of space between them.

test_cases.action: Open the 'general' room and tap the smiling face in the message box to open the picture panel. Tap 'GIFs'. Drag the small handle at the top of the panel upward so the panel fills the screen. Tap 'Trending GIFs' and say where you are. Then use the small back arrow to return to the GIFs list, tap the panel's search box, type hello, and say where you are again. Do not tap any picture. Press Back once to close.
test_cases.real_if: at those points you cannot find anything on the screen that tells you where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: you can find something on the screen that tells you where you are
test_cases.observed_result: In '# general' I tapped the smiling face and then 'GIFs', and dragged the handle up so the panel filled the screen. On the GIFs list, each tile carries a word ('Trending GIFs', 'hello', 'lol', and so on), which I could manage. I tapped 'Trending GIFs'. The panel then showed a small back arrow and the word 'Trending' under the Emoji / GIFs / Stickers row with 'GIFs' shaded, and '# general' faintly visible, dimmed, at the very top. So something did tell me where I was. But everything below it was a moving wall of faces, sportsmen, a mascot and large captions like 'THE RECKONING IS COMING', and I had to force myself to look only at the top line. I used the small back arrow, tapped the search box and typed hello. There was no heading now, only my word 'hello' in the box, 'GIFs' shaded above it, and '# general' dimmed at the top. Below that were more faces, animals and big 'Hello' captions. I pressed Back once and it only closed the keyboard, so I pressed Back again a few seconds later and the panel closed, back to '# general'.

s43.closing_comment: There is a small 'Trending' label and a dimmed '# general', so something names the place, but the wall of moving faces and captions still overloads me before I can use it.
